distractors.reason: We don't say 'big language'. 'Big' describes size, not the level of formality of language.
We don't say 'high language' in this sense. 'High' is used with temperature, prices or standards, not with register.
'Serious language' describes the content or tone, not the formal register. The standard collocation is 'formal language'.

example_sentence: Your letter should be written in ___ language, not slang.
l1_interference: Polacy mogą dosłownie przełożyć 'duży' i powiedzieć 'big language' zamiast poprawnego 'formal language'. Warto zapamiętać, że 'formal' oznacza oficjalny rejestr języka.
explanation: In English, 'formal' is the standard adjective for language that follows official or polite conventions, in contrast to casual or slang language.

related_collocations.example: We had a casual conversation over coffee.
She made a polite request for more time.
The email had an informal tone, so I replied in the same way.

memory_tip: FORMAL = official, polite register (letters, meetings, reports) | CASUAL/INFORMAL = relaxed register (friends, chats, slang)
